 Cade Cunningham led the Pistons with 33 points (8-of-20 FGs, 14-of-14 FTs), five rebounds, eight assists, one steal, one block and three three-pointers in a 137-117 loss to the Heat on Saturday.
 It wasn’t a great encore after his performance on Thursday, but Cunningham still led the way for Detroit. 12 of his points came in the fourth quarter, though it wasn’t enough to complete a comeback. Cade has been effective from the free throw line all season, but he has been on fire lately. Over his last three games, he has shot 34-of-35 from the charity stripe. Unfortunately, he wasn’t quite as dominant as he was on Thursday. Still, Cade has been well worth the first-round pick.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Cade Cunningham led the Pistons with 52 points (16-of-25 FGs, 17-of-18 FTs), five rebounds, 11 assists, one steal, one block and three three-pointers in a 144-140 double overtime win over the Wizards on Thursday. 
 Cunningham set a new career high for scoring in this game, with 30 of those 52 coming in the fourth quarter and overtime. However, the most impressive part of his performance was that he didn’t turn the ball over once, which led to him becoming the first player with at least 50 points and 10 assists in a game without turning it over. This was one of the best games anyone has had this season, and it came after he scored a total of 31 points over Detroit’s last two games. It was good to see him not only get back on track, but to truly dominate. He’ll look to carry some of this production with him to Miami on Saturday to wrap up the week. 
 Cade Cunningham 
 DET 
 Guard 
 #2 
 Cade Cunningham posted 17 points (7-of-16 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), three rebounds, seven assists and one steal over 27 minutes in Monday’s win over the Wizards. 
 Cunningham turned in his second consecutive lackluster shooting performance, going 0-for-4 from three-point range while attempting 16 shots or fewer for just the fourth time this season. He poured in 11 first-half points and played a season-low 27 minutes during the second game of a back-to-back for Detroit. This looks like a relatively minor blip on the radar as he works through a shooting slump. He’ll get a couple days off before the Pistons square off with the Wizards in a rematch on Thursday. 
 Cade Cunningham

 Guard 
 #2 
 Cade Cunningham totaled 14 points (6-of-15 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, eight assists and two steals across 38 minutes in Sunday’s loss to the Lakers. 
 Cunningham was held without a basket in the first half as he cobbled together an uncharacteristically poor shooting performance, finishing just 1-of-6 from three-point range. He managed to somewhat salvage the effort from a fantasy perspective by still getting to double digits while also dishing out eight assists. He’ll attempt to get back on track when the Pistons kick off a three-game week with a pair of matchups against the lowly Wizards before facing the Heat in a road tilt.

 Cade Cunningham had 26 points (9-of-22 FGs, 7-of-7 FTs), seven rebounds, 11 assists, two blocks, two steals and one three-pointer against the 76ers on Wednesday. 
 Cunningham continues to make an impact on the defensive end early in the season as he recorded two blocks and two steals against the 76ers Wednesday. The 25-year-old point guard also scored 26 points on the offensive end, though he went 1-of-9 on three-point attempts. The Pistons are off until Sunday’s game against the Lakers. 
 Cade Cunningham 
 DET 
 Guard 
 #2 
 Cade Cunningham had 33 points (13-of-20 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), five rebounds, seven assists, five steals and four three-pointers in the Pistons’ 124-91 victory over the Hornets on Monday. 
 Cunningham has now recorded at least 30 points, at least five rebounds, at least seven assists, at least two steals and at least four three-pointers in two of his last three games. Due to his efficiency and five steals, Monday was the 25-year-old point guard’s best game of the young season so far. With Jalen Duren (hamstring) still sidelined, expect the Pistons to continue to lean on Cunningham even more than they usually do.

 Cunningham had just 19 points in Tuesday’s loss to the Knicks, but bounced back with 30 points in the victory over the Hornets Wednesday. Expect Cunningham to continue doing it all for the Pistons and he should keep shouldering a heavy usage load while Jalen Duren (hamstring) is out.

 Cade Cunningham amassed 19 points (7-of-18 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), nine rebounds, eight assists, one block and two three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Knicks. 
 Given Cunningham’s scoring trend in Detroit’s first four games, he’s likely to score 20+ against the Hornets on Wednesday. The Knicks kept him in check for most of the night, with Cade totaling 10 points in the final three quarters of Tuesday’s defeat. The good news for fantasy managers was that he put up quality rebound and assist numbers, finishing one board and two helpers shy of a triple-double. 
 Cade Cunningham 
 DET 
 Guard

 Cade Cunningham finished Sunday’s win over the 76ers with 26 points (9-of-19 FGs, 5-of-8 FTs), eight rebounds, eight assists, two steals, two blocks and three three-pointers. 
 Cunningham and the Pistons remained undefeated after defeating the 76ers, doing so without two starters. With Jalen Duren out for at least two weeks and Ausar Thompson also unavailable on Sunday, Cunningham will have to do more of the heavy lifting for the Pistons in the short term. Beyond scoring, he provided excellent value for fantasy managers across the board. The Pistons play three games in Week 2, starting with the Knicks on Tuesday. 
 Cade Cunningham 
 DET 
 Guard 
 #2 
 Cade Cunningham had 16 points (5-of-8 FGs, 4-of-6 FTs), two rebounds, eight assists, one steal, three blocks and two three-pointers in the Pistons’ 128-111 victory over the Heat on Friday. 
 Cunningham had another fine game as he filled the stat sheet and led the Pistons to another win to start the season. However, after turning the ball over five times in the win over the Celtics on Tuesday, he had seven turnovers against the Heat on Friday. Even opposing coaches like the Heat’s Erik Spolstra have pointed out that Cunningham isn’t necessarily a bad ball-handler, but commits a lot of turnovers thanks to almost always having the ball in his hands. That doesn’t offer much comfort to fantasy managers with Cunningham in nine-category leagues as he’s likely to be towards the top of the league in turnovers this year. 
 Cade Cunningham 
 DET 
 Guard

 Cade Cunningham put up 14 points (5-of-11 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), two rebounds, nine assists, one steal, and two 3-pointers in 25 minutes against the Timberwolves. 
 Cade looked like his usual self as the primary creator of the offense. It is important to note the nine assists to the five turnovers he had. Detroit lost some ball handling this summer which will put even more responsibility on Cade. It would not be a shock if he leads the league in turnovers this year because he’s the only starter that can handle the ball.

 Davion Mitchell posted a full line on Saturday with 15 points (4-of-7 FGs), four rebounds, nine assists, two steals, two blocks and three three-pointers against the Pistons.
 Fresh off dropping a career high 17 assists on Friday, Mitchell wasn’t able to record another double-double, but he came close. He ended up making up for it by contributing extra value on the defensive end in what has been arguably his best two-game stretch of the season. He has been one of the best late-round picks in fantasy basketball this season and should continue to stuff the stat sheet as Miami’s starting point guard for the rest of the season.

 Giannis Antetokounmpo led the Heat with 34 points (13-of-17 FGs), 14 rebounds, eight assists, one steal, three blocks and one three-pointer in a 137-117 win over the Pistons on Saturday.
 Giannis wasn’t able to match his season high of 37 points that he set on Friday, but he was able to score at least 30 points for a third straight game, which led to Miami’s fourth straight win. Detroit didn’t have much of an answer for him, which helped him add an efficient shooting night to a dominant stat line. Plus, he was able to have an effective night at the free throw line, which helped inflate his value.

 Klay Thompson returned to the lineup on Saturday and contributed 26 points (10-of-17 FGs), one rebound, four assists, one block and six three-pointers against the Pistons.
 Following a one-game absence, Thompson was back in the starting unit for the Heat and had another strong outing. This was his second-highest scoring performance of the year, and he has really shrugged off a slow start. Over his last seven games, he has averaged 20.7 points and 5.1 triples per game while shooting 50 percent from the floor and 46.8 percent from deep. If he continues to shoot this well, Miami should keep winning more games.

 Duncan Robinson finished with 10 points (3-of-8 FGs), one rebound, one assist and two three-pointers against the Heat on Saturday.
 Robinson exited this game late in the second quarter due to thigh soreness and didn’t end up returning. Kevin Huerter replaced him to start the second half, and if Robinson remains out in San Antonio on Tuesday, Huerter would likely get the start. Robinson has been a big part of Detroit’s success this season, but Huerter is a solid replacement that has been on fire lately.

 Kevin Huerter provided a boost off the bench with 20 points (9-of-15 FGs), four rebounds, seven assists, one steal, three blocks and two three-pointers against the Heat on Saturday.
 Huerter has been fantastic off the bench for Detroit lately, and he filled up the box score once again in this one.  Sharpe started the year off slow, but he’s really starting to show why he was one of the best late-round targets.  Matas Buzelis delivered 18 points (5-of-9 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), nine rebounds and two assists over 30 minutes to propel the Bulls to a 117-106 win over the Timberwolves on Saturday.
 Buzelis has gotten off to a rocky start overall this season, but he looked sharp in the early stages of this one, pouring in a game-high 14 points on 5-of-6 shooting, including 2-of-3 from beyond the arc, in the opening half. He cooled off considerably afterwards, notching just four points in the entire second half. Still, he managed to do enough as Chicago’s primary offensive creator in place of injured rookie sensation Caleb Wilson, who is set to miss 4-6 weeks with a fractured right hand, to power them to a much-needed road win. It’s hard to trust him for fantasy purposes given how up-and-down he’s been, but he should get plenty of scoring chances while Wilson is sidelined for at least the next month.
